2026-09-12-audit-changes-02/executing#3.reason: Narrow it. A policy waiver resolves for the scan's CANONICAL rule as before; a waiver naming a rule the scan enforces but cannot attribute is REFUSED loudly (LedgerError, the direction apply_ledger already takes when a text scan meets an arg_type predicate) rather than silently disabling the whole scan. And the docstring's known-limit paragraph is rewritten: it books the sibling withdrawal as pre-existing when this change CREATED it - before it, a waiver on the non-canonical rule did nothing, so nothing could be withdrawn. That is the laundering shape, in my own prose, and correcting the text is part of the fix, not a footnote to it.

2026-09-12-audit-changes-02/executing#5.reason: Tighten and measure. CLAIM_TOOL_ID admits a bare gbg <word> and CLAIM_QUANTIFIER admits all, any and only, so ordinary prose that merely mentions a verb is swept in; the conjunction moves to the same clause, or to a universal governing a named rule or verb. The new CLAIM_EXIT alternative matches any digit 0-3 within 60 characters of the phrase, including the trailing digit of a larger number, and is anchored accordingly. And the number that decides affordability is the per-lane discharge count, which the change set never measured - only the corpus-wide ratio.

2026-09-12-audit-changes-02/under-reject.reason: Admit narrowly. GBG_ROUND excuses a round from EVERY per-round refusal the gate makes, including :committed, where the rc permission needs only the :open kind tolerated. The admission also runs for a final release, where it is harmless only because release_fails refuses on an open round first - relying on another guard's ordering is not the guarantee the comment claims. Next change set: admit only on the rc path, and only the refusal kind the permission is for.

2026-09-12-audit-changes-02/under-reject.reason: Make the guard name the object the verb acts on. running_dev() tests the RUNNING copy while root is what gets tagged and pushed, so after this change the check and the action can refer to different checkouts. Either re-derive it from the argument (ispath(joinpath(root, .git))) or give only release_fails the root keyword, which is what all but one of the new tests actually exercise. The docstring's defence that the CLI never passes it is a statement about one caller, not a guard.

2026-09-12-audit-changes-02/behaviour-ch.reason: The blocker, and it leads. gbg round scripts grants a general mid-round unfreeze for any round at any point, where the motivating case was narrow: a round whose own finding is an unparseable verifier cannot verify itself. Next change set scopes it to that case and records the relaxation where the invariant is documented - the protocols and ARCHITECTURE still describe preflight as the moment the scripts are fixed. The new docstring is itself false on this point: it asserts copy_scripts runs there and nowhere else, in the body of the second function that runs it.

2026-09-12-audit-changes-02/executing#7.reason: Correct or remove the figures. Three of four measurements cited in the new comments do not reproduce, and one counts homes this diff created. This lane exists because a measurement written into a comment is certified by every later reader, and I have spent this round being convicted of exactly that - a written account of a thing being less reliable than re-measuring it.

2026-09-12-audit-changes-02/claim-versus.reason: Complete both migrations and correct both claims. 2026-09-12-audit-changes-02/over-rejecti.reason: Recording the verdict is the right mechanism, and the verb's contract did not move with it. Rounds.build is documented as run, log, return the code; it now persists {code, head, at} into ROUND.toml and re-validates the WHOLE record through save, so a record the current schema rejects makes a previously working verb throw a RoundError instead of building - which is exactly the migration case for any round open across this change. Next change set: the docstring says what the verb now writes and what it validates, the guide's three mentions follow it, and a test exercises build over a record that fails validation, since the new testset pins only the fresh, valid one.
